question: What is the main purpose of the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: To demonstrate basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position in relation to other objects
choice_b: To evaluate parallel parking on a public street
choice_c: To test highway speed control only
choice_d: To test knowledge of air brake systems only
explanation: The manual states the Basic Control Skills test requires you to demonstrate basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position in relation to other objects.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: For what four things will you receive points during the Basic Control Skills test exercises?
choice_a: Changing direction to gain a better position, crossing over or touching boundary lines or cones, and your final position
choice_b: Number of gear changes used
choice_c: Speed, fuel efficiency, and tire wear
choice_d: Time to complete the course only
explanation: The manual states you will receive points for changing direction to gain a better position, crossing over or touching boundary lines or cones, and for your final position.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: What must you do when entering or exiting the vehicle during backing exercises?
choice_a: Face away from the vehicle while exiting to see traffic better
choice_b: Turn off the engine completely and remove the keys
choice_c: Leave the engine running in drive and step out quickly
choice_d: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times
explanation: The manual requires you to set your parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three (3) points of contact at all times.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: On a bus, what is required instead of the standard entering/exiting procedure during backing exercises?
choice_a: Exit backward down the steps
choice_b: Have a passenger spot the vehicle
choice_c: Exit only through the rear emergency door
choice_d: Face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail
explanation: The manual specifies that when entering/exiting a bus, you should face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: What are the four exercises included in the Basic Control Skills test, in order?
choice_a: Straight-Line Backing, Forward Stop, Reverse Offset Backing, and Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: Forward Stop, Reverse Offset Backing, Straight-Line Backing, and Forward Offset Tracking
choice_c: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, and Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: Parallel Parking, Alley Dock, Straight Backing, and Sight-Side Backing
explanation: The manual lists Step 1 - Forward Stop, Step 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: Where may the Basic Control Skills test exercises be conducted?
choice_a: Either off-road or somewhere on the street during the Road test
choice_b: Only at the DMV office garage
choice_c: Only on the interstate highway
choice_d: Only in a closed parking lot
explanation: The manual states the Basic Control Skills test will include the exercises either off-road or somewhere on the street during the Road test.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: What is a "pull-up" during a Basic Control Skills backing exercise?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_b: Pulling the vehicle completely out of the exercise area
choice_c: Backing up faster than instructed
choice_d: Pulling the parking brake handle
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: On which two exercises are pull-ups scored?
choice_a: Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing
choice_c: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_d: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
explanation: The manual states pull-ups apply to Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: Does stopping without changing direction count as a pull-up?
choice_a: No, stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up
choice_b: Only during Exercise 4
choice_c: Only if it happens more than twice
choice_d: Yes, any stop counts as a pull-up
explanation: The manual explicitly states that stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: Are you penalized for initial pull-ups during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Yes, but only during Exercise 2
choice_b: Yes, every pull-up results in immediate failure
choice_c: No, pull-ups are never counted at all
choice_d: No, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is an "encroachment" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Driving faster than 5 mph during the exercise
choice_b: Taking more than two minutes to complete an exercise
choice_c: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of your vehicle, other than the mirrors or certain unique vehicle parts
choice_d: Failing to sound the horn at the end of an exercise
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of your vehicle, other than the vehicle's mirrors (door or fender) or other unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: Are unique vehicle parts below door mirror height counted as an encroachment if they touch a boundary?
choice_a: Yes, but only on Exercise 1
choice_b: No, only mirrors are ever counted
choice_c: No, only tires are ever counted
choice_d: Yes, unique parts below door mirror height are counted as an encroachment
explanation: The manual states that unique parts below door mirror height are counted as an encroachment (unlike unique parts at or higher than door mirror height, such as a bucket truck).
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What must you do if you have encroached during an exercise?
choice_a: Reverse the entire exercise and start over
choice_b: Stop immediately when signaled by the examiner and return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries
choice_c: Continue the exercise and ignore the encroachment
choice_d: Immediately exit the vehicle and end the test
explanation: The manual states that if you have encroached, the examiner will stop you and you must return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries, stopping immediately when signaled by the examiner.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How does the examiner score encroachments?
choice_a: By counting the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone, with each encroachment counting as an error
choice_b: By averaging all encroachments across all four exercises into one score
choice_c: By deducting time from your overall test
choice_d: By only recording the first encroachment of the test
explanation: The manual states the examiner will score the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone, and each encroachment will count as an error.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is scored as a "look" during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Looking at the examiner for instructions
choice_b: Glancing at the rearview mirror once
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing
choice_d: Checking the speedometer
explanation: The manual defines a look as exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What must you do before safely exiting the vehicle to check its position (a "look")?
choice_a: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral/park
choice_b: Turn off the headlights only
choice_c: Shift into reverse and leave the engine running
choice_d: Sound the horn three times
explanation: The manual states that when exiting to check the vehicle's position, you must set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral/park.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many points of contact must you maintain when exiting or entering the vehicle during an exercise?
choice_a: Four (4) points of contact at all times
choice_b: Two (2) points of contact at all times
choice_c: Three (3) points of contact at all times
choice_d: One (1) point of contact is sufficient
explanation: The manual requires you to maintain three (3) points of contact with the vehicle at all times when exiting/entering.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What may happen if you do not safely secure the vehicle or safely exit/enter it during a look?
choice_a: The examiner will give you a warning with no other consequence
choice_b: The exercise is repeated from the beginning at no cost
choice_c: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_d: You simply lose one point
explanation: The manual warns that failing to safely secure or exit/enter the vehicle may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What happens if you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral/park)?
choice_a: It is ignored if you close it quickly
choice_b: It only counts as a pull-up
choice_c: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_d: It is simply counted as one look with no other consequence
explanation: The manual states that if you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: On a bus, what action counts as a "look"?
choice_a: Walking to the back of the bus to get a better view
choice_b: Adjusting the mirrors from the driver's seat
choice_c: Turning on the interior lights
choice_d: Honking the horn
explanation: The manual states that on a bus, if you walk to the back of the bus to get a better view, it will count as a look.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: A maximum of one (1) free look
choice_b: No free looks are allowed
choice_c: A maximum of three (3) free looks
choice_d: A maximum of two (2) free looks
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One (1) free look
choice_b: Two (2) free looks
choice_c: Three (3) free looks
choice_d: Zero free looks
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing to check the position of your vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills Scoring - Final Position
question: On which two exercises is final vehicle position scored?
choice_a: Only Exercise 1 - Forward Stop
choice_b: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_c: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: All four exercises equally
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills Scoring - Final Position
question: What three actions must you take upon completion of an exercise?
choice_a: Honk twice, flash the headlights, and roll down the window
choice_b: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_c: Shift into reverse, apply the brake, and open the door
choice_d: Turn off the engine, exit the vehicle, and wave to the examiner
explanation: The manual states that upon completion of an exercise, you must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn indicating you have completed the exercise.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills Scoring - Final Position
question: What happens if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner?
choice_a: You are given unlimited extra attempts
choice_b: Nothing, since final position is only a suggestion
choice_c: You will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
choice_d: Only a warning is issued with no scoring impact
explanation: The manual warns that if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, you will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills - Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: What may result from failing to follow the examiner's instructions for completing an exercise as directed?
choice_a: A requirement to repeat only that portion later that day
choice_b: A minor deduction of one point only
choice_c: No consequence as long as you finish the exercise eventually
choice_d: An automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner
explanation: The manual states that failure to follow examiner instructions for completing the exercise as directed may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills - Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: Which of the following is given as an example of an "unsafe act" during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Asking the examiner a clarifying question
choice_b: Using one free pull-up during Exercise 2
choice_c: Taking slightly longer than average to complete an exercise
choice_d: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion
explanation: The manual gives forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion as examples of committing an unsafe act.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills - Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: What should you do if you do not understand the examiner's instructions for completing an exercise?
choice_a: Guess and proceed without asking
choice_b: Ask the examiner for clarification
choice_c: Wait silently until the examiner repeats it unprompted
choice_d: Refuse to continue the test
explanation: The manual instructs that if you do not understand the instructions or how to complete the exercises, you should ask the examiner for clarification.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills - Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: If permitted, what may you ask the examiner to do before an exercise?
choice_a: Walk you through the exercise area
choice_b: Skip the exercise entirely
choice_c: Perform the exercise for you as a demonstration drive
choice_d: Provide the exact score you will receive in advance
explanation: The manual notes that, if permitted, you may ask the examiner to walk you through the exercise area.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What does Exercise 1 - Forward Stop require you to demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to merge onto an expressway
choice_b: Your ability to back the vehicle in a straight line
choice_c: Your ability to parallel park
choice_d: Your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a controlled stop
explanation: The manual states Exercise 1 - Forward Stop demonstrates your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a controlled stop.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: How many times may you stop during Exercise 1 - Forward Stop?
choice_a: You may stop only once
choice_b: You may stop as many times as needed
choice_c: You may stop up to two times
choice_d: You may not stop at all before the box
explanation: The manual states that in Exercise 1 you may stop only once.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 1, what vehicle parts are excluded when judging whether the front of the vehicle is within the stop box?
choice_a: Unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height, such as a bucket truck
choice_b: The headlights only
choice_c: The front bumper only
choice_d: Nothing is excluded; every part of the vehicle counts
explanation: The manual excludes unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height, such as a bucket truck, from the front-most part measurement.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: What three actions do you take once you have stopped in Exercise 1?
choice_a: Open the door, wave, and wait for the examiner to approach
choice_b: Set your parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_c: Flash your headlights, honk once, and roll forward slightly
choice_d: Turn off the engine, exit, and check the tires
explanation: The manual states that when you have stopped, you set your parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and sound the horn.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: Who points out the front-most part of your vehicle when giving instructions for Exercise 1?
choice_a: The vehicle's owner's manual
choice_b: Your examiner
choice_c: A fellow test-taker
choice_d: You must determine it yourself with no guidance
explanation: The manual states your examiner will point out the front-most part of your vehicle when giving instructions for this exercise.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: What does Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing require you to demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to back a vehicle in a straight line
choice_b: Your ability to steer around cones while moving forward
choice_c: Your ability to parallel park at the curb
choice_d: Your ability to complete a controlled forward stop
explanation: The manual states Exercise 2 demonstrates your ability to back a vehicle in a straight line.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 2, until where must you back the vehicle straight through the alley?
choice_a: Until the examiner sounds a horn
choice_b: For exactly 50 feet regardless of cone position
choice_c: Until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley
choice_d: Until the rear tires touch the outer boundary line
explanation: The manual instructs you to back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What three things are you scored on during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Steering smoothness and gear selection
choice_b: Looks only
choice_c: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_d: Speed, mirror use, and horn timing
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position on Exercise 2.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are you allowed during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Three (3) free pull-ups
choice_b: Zero free pull-ups
choice_c: One (1) free pull-up
choice_d: Two (2) free pull-ups
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one (1) free pull-up during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How many times may you safely exit the vehicle to check around it during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: You may not exit the vehicle at all during this exercise
choice_b: Three (3) times
choice_c: Only one (1) time
choice_d: Two (2) times
explanation: The manual states you may safely exit the vehicle only one (1) time to check around the vehicle during Exercise 2.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What does Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking require you to demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to perform a U-turn
choice_b: Your ability to make a controlled stop at a specific point
choice_c: Your ability to back a vehicle into a tight space
choice_d: Your ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward without stopping
explanation: The manual states Exercise 3 demonstrates your ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward without stopping.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3, which direction do you initially steer through the opening?
choice_a: Straight, without any steering input
choice_b: In reverse, backing through the opening
choice_c: Right, staying in the original lane
choice_d: Left, into the opposite lane
explanation: The manual instructs you to drive forward and steer to the left through the opening into the opposite lane.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What tire clearance are you scored on in Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Keeping the rear tires at least six feet from any cone
choice_b: Keeping the right-most rear tire between the cone and the line
choice_c: Keeping all four tires exactly centered in the lane
choice_d: Keeping the left front tire off the curb
explanation: The manual states you must keep the right-most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping, and are scored on forward tracking clearance.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Are you allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: No, you are NOT allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during this exercise
choice_b: Yes, you may stop once if needed to reposition
choice_c: Yes, exiting is allowed but stopping is not
choice_d: Yes, you may back up but not exit
explanation: The manual explicitly states you are NOT allowed to stop, back-up, or exit the vehicle during Exercise 3.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What happens if you stop during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: You are given a warning and may restart from the beginning
choice_b: The exercise will be ended
choice_c: Nothing, since stopping is permitted once
choice_d: You simply receive one pull-up and continue
explanation: The manual states that if you stop during Exercise 3, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Where must you stop your vehicle at the end of Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Anywhere within the alley, position does not matter
choice_b: Parallel to the outer boundary and prior to or at the cones at the far end of the exercise
choice_c: Exactly ten feet past the last cone
choice_d: At a 45-degree angle to the outer boundary
explanation: The manual instructs you to stop your vehicle when you are parallel to the outer boundary and prior to or at the cones at the far end of the exercise.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What does Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing require you to demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to offset back and park a vehicle at the end of an alley
choice_b: Your ability to merge into expressway traffic
choice_c: Your ability to perform a controlled forward stop
choice_d: Your ability to drive forward through a narrow opening
explanation: The manual states Exercise 4 demonstrates your ability to offset back and park a vehicle at the end of an alley.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: In Exercise 4, within how many feet of the rear of the alley must the rear-most part of your vehicle come to rest?
choice_a: Within three (3) feet
choice_b: Within ten (10) feet
choice_c: Within five (5) feet
choice_d: Within one (1) foot
explanation: The manual states you must bring the rear-most part of your vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must you do if you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4?
choice_a: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, before resuming the exercise
choice_b: Immediately end the test with an automatic failure
choice_c: Exit the vehicle and manually push it back into position
choice_d: Continue backing until you reach the boundary again
explanation: The manual states that if you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley, you will be required to pull straight forward past the alley entrance until you are signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are you allowed during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One (1) free pull-up
choice_b: Zero free pull-ups
choice_c: Two (2) free pull-ups
choice_d: Three (3) free pull-ups
explanation: The manual states you are allowed two (2) free pull-ups during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What is the maximum number of times you may exit the vehicle to check around it during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: You may not exit the vehicle at all
choice_b: A maximum of three (3) times
choice_c: A maximum of one (1) time
choice_d: A maximum of two (2) times
explanation: The manual states you may exit the vehicle a maximum of two (2) times to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must be true of your vehicle's position within the alley when Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing is completed?
choice_a: Only the front of the vehicle needs to be within boundaries
choice_b: Your vehicle may be angled up to 30 degrees
choice_c: Your vehicle must be straight within the alley and completely within the defined exercise boundaries
choice_d: The vehicle may extend beyond the outer boundary line by up to one foot
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must be straight within the alley when completed and must be completely within the defined exercise boundaries; you may not go beyond the outer boundary line.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What three things are you scored on during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Mirror adjustment, seatbelt use, and steering grip
choice_b: Looks only, since it is the last exercise
choice_c: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_d: Speed, gear selection, and horn use
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position on Exercise 4.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: Which of the following is required of you at all times during the On-Road driving test?
choice_a: Wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_b: Keep the radio on for the examiner
choice_c: Maintain exactly the speed limit at all times regardless of conditions
choice_d: Use only the left lane throughout the test
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: What must you complete the On-Road driving test without?
choice_a: Any use of turn signals
choice_b: An accident or moving violation
choice_c: Any stops of any kind
choice_d: Any lane changes
explanation: The manual states you must complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: On what two things will the examiner be scoring you during the driving test?
choice_a: Only the time taken to complete the route
choice_b: Fuel economy and vehicle cleanliness
choice_c: Only your final parking position
choice_d: Specific driving maneuvers as well as your general driving behavior
explanation: The manual states the examiner will be scoring you on specific driving maneuvers as well as on your general driving behavior.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: What happens if your test route does not include a certain traffic situation?
choice_a: You may be asked to simulate it by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_b: You automatically receive full points for that maneuver
choice_c: That portion of the test is simply skipped with no substitute
choice_d: The test is automatically rescheduled
explanation: The manual states that if your test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate a traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: Will you be asked to drive in an unsafe manner during the test?
choice_a: No, you will not be asked to drive in an unsafe manner
choice_b: Yes, occasionally to test your reaction
choice_c: Only during the expressway portion
choice_d: Only if you request it
explanation: The manual states you will not be asked to drive in an unsafe manner and directions will be given with plenty of time to comply.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: What defines "unsafe coasting" while approaching a turn?
choice_a: Coasting for any distance whatsoever
choice_b: When your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
choice_c: Coasting for more than one city block
choice_d: Any time your speed drops below 10 mph
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: If you must stop before making a turn, how should you stop?
choice_a: Come to a smooth stop without skidding, behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign
choice_b: Stop anywhere convenient near the intersection
choice_c: Brake as hard as possible to stop instantly
choice_d: Coast to a stop with the clutch depressed the entire time
explanation: The manual instructs that if you must stop before making the turn, come to a smooth stop without skidding and stop behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before a turn, where should you stop?
choice_a: At least two full car lengths back regardless of visibility
choice_b: Exactly at the stop line, ignoring the vehicle ahead
choice_c: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead to save space
choice_d: Where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you (a safe gap)
explanation: The manual instructs that if stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: While waiting to turn, which direction should your front wheels be aimed?
choice_a: Straight ahead
choice_b: Turned away from the direction of the turn
choice_c: Already turned toward the direction of the turn
choice_d: It does not matter as long as the vehicle does not roll
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead while waiting to turn, and to not let your vehicle roll.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: During the turn itself, what should you keep checking via your mirror?
choice_a: That the fuel gauge has not changed
choice_b: That the radio volume is appropriate
choice_c: That the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn
choice_d: That the trailer doors remain closed
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep checking your mirror to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: Where should the vehicle finish after completing a turn?
choice_a: In whichever lane is closest regardless of direction of travel
choice_b: Straddling the center line briefly before merging
choice_c: In the correct lane, without moving into oncoming traffic
choice_d: In the leftmost lane only
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should not move into oncoming traffic and should finish the turn in the correct lane.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: After completing a turn, what should you do regarding your turn signal and lane position?
choice_a: Immediately move to the left-most lane
choice_b: Make sure the turn signal is off, get up to speed of traffic, and move into the right-most lane when safe if not already there
choice_c: Turn off the hazard lights only
choice_d: Leave the turn signal on until the next turn
explanation: The manual states that after the turn you should make sure the turn signal is off, get up to speed of traffic using a turn signal, and move into the right-most lane when safe to do so if not already there.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As you approach an intersection and must stop, what must you avoid doing to the vehicle?
choice_a: You must not signal your stop
choice_b: You must not let it roll forward or backward
choice_c: You must not check your mirrors
choice_d: You must not use the parking brake
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must not roll forward or backward when stopped at an intersection.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: When driving through an intersection, what must you decelerate and yield to?
choice_a: Only oncoming left-turning vehicles
choice_b: Any pedestrians and traffic in the intersection
choice_c: Only vehicles with their hazard lights on
choice_d: Nothing, since you have the right of way once moving
explanation: The manual instructs that when driving through an intersection, you should decelerate and yield to any pedestrians and traffic in the intersection.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: Are you permitted to change lanes while proceeding through an intersection?
choice_a: Yes, as long as you signal first
choice_b: Yes, but only to the right
choice_c: No, you should not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_d: Yes, but only if traffic is light
explanation: The manual instructs you not to change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: Once through an intersection, what should you do?
choice_a: Continue checking mirrors and traffic, and accelerate smoothly, changing gears as necessary
choice_b: Accelerate as quickly as possible regardless of gear
choice_c: Immediately stop to check for damage
choice_d: Turn off your turn signal only, with no other action needed
explanation: The manual states that once through the intersection, you should continue checking mirrors and traffic and accelerate smoothly, changing gears as necessary.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, where should your vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: As far left as possible at all times
choice_b: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane)
choice_c: Centered on the lane line
choice_d: Straddling two lanes to maximize visibility
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) during the Urban Business portion of the test.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, what is expected of you regarding traffic checks and following distance?
choice_a: Make regular traffic checks and maintain a safe following distance
choice_b: Check traffic only at intersections
choice_c: Follow the vehicle ahead as closely as safely possible to keep pace
choice_d: Ignore following distance in favor of speed
explanation: The manual states that during this part of the test, you are expected to make regular traffic checks and maintain a safe following distance.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: In the Urban Business portion, should you exceed the posted speed limit to keep up with the flow of traffic?
choice_a: The posted speed limit does not apply during the test
choice_b: No, you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit
choice_c: Yes, exceeding the limit slightly is acceptable to match traffic flow
choice_d: Yes, as long as the examiner does not object
explanation: The manual states you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: During the multiple-lane portion of the on-road test, what lane change sequence are you asked to perform?
choice_a: Weave between three lanes continuously
choice_b: Change lanes twice to the left in a row
choice_c: Change lanes to the left, and then back to the right
choice_d: Change lanes to the right only
explanation: The manual states that during multiple lane portions of the test, you will be asked to change lanes to the left, and then back to the right.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: What should you do first before changing lanes during the test?
choice_a: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals
choice_b: Speed up first to create a gap
choice_c: Activate the turn signal first, then check traffic
choice_d: Honk the horn to alert nearby vehicles
explanation: The manual instructs you to make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: How should you execute a lane change once traffic checks and signaling are complete?
choice_a: Change lanes as abruptly as possible to minimize exposure time
choice_b: Smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so
choice_c: Change lanes only if another vehicle signals permission
choice_d: Wait for the examiner to physically steer the vehicle
explanation: The manual states you should smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so, after making traffic checks and using proper signals.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Before entering an expressway or rural/limited access highway, what should you do?
choice_a: Accelerate to maximum speed before checking traffic
choice_b: Merge without signaling to avoid distracting other drivers
choice_c: Stop at the end of the entrance ramp before merging
choice_d: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
explanation: The manual instructs that before entering the expressway, you should check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the expressway, what three things should you maintain?
choice_a: Maximum speed, minimum following distance, and left-lane travel
choice_b: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed
choice_c: Hazard lights, low beams, and horn readiness
choice_d: Constant lane changes to keep pace with traffic
explanation: The manual states that once on the expressway, you should maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: When exiting the expressway, what should you do?
choice_a: Accelerate through the exit ramp to merge quickly
choice_b: Decelerate while still in the main travel lane before reaching the exit lane
choice_c: Make necessary traffic checks, use proper signals, and decelerate smoothly in the exit lane
choice_d: Turn off your headlights before exiting
explanation: The manual instructs that when exiting the expressway, you should make necessary traffic checks, use proper signals, and decelerate smoothly in the exit lane.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the exit ramp, what must you continue to do?
choice_a: Decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles
choice_b: Straddle the lane markings to have more room
choice_c: Stop completely regardless of traffic conditions
choice_d: Accelerate back to expressway speed immediately
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: What should you continue doing throughout your time on the expressway, in addition to maintaining lane position and speed?
choice_a: Continue to check the fuel gauge every few minutes
choice_b: Continue to sound the horn periodically
choice_c: Continue to check traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_d: Continue to flash your headlights at other vehicles
explanation: The manual states that once on the expressway, you should continue to check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: What does the Stop/Start maneuver on the on-road test simulate?
choice_a: Coming to a complete stop at a red light
choice_b: Pulling the vehicle over to the side of the road and stopping as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle
choice_c: Stopping at a weigh station for inspection
choice_d: Stopping to allow a pedestrian to cross at a crosswalk
explanation: The manual states that for the Stop/Start maneuver, you will be asked to pull your vehicle over to the side of the road and stop as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Where should you move your vehicle for the Stop/Start maneuver?
choice_a: Any lane, as position does not matter
choice_b: The right-most lane or shoulder of the road
choice_c: The center turn lane
choice_d: The left-most lane
explanation: The manual instructs you to check traffic thoroughly in all directions and move to the right-most lane or shoulder of the road for this maneuver.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: As you prepare for the Stop/Start maneuver, which turn signal should you activate?
choice_a: Both turn signals simultaneously
choice_b: The left turn signal
choice_c: The right turn signal
choice_d: No signal is required for this maneuver
explanation: The manual states that as you prepare for the stop, you should activate your right turn signal.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: How should you bring your vehicle to a stop during the Stop/Start maneuver?
choice_a: Allow the vehicle to roll slightly past the intended point
choice_b: Coast to a gradual stop with the clutch depressed
choice_c: Brake as hard as possible for a quick stop
choice_d: Bring your vehicle to a full stop without coasting
explanation: The manual instructs you to decelerate smoothly, brake evenly, change gears as necessary, and bring your vehicle to a full stop without coasting.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, what must be true of your vehicle's position?
choice_a: It must straddle the shoulder and the travel lane
choice_b: It must be angled 45 degrees away from the curb
choice_c: It must be positioned in the center of the road
choice_d: It must be parallel to the curb or shoulder of the road and safely out of the traffic flow
explanation: The manual states that once stopped, your vehicle must be parallel to the curb or shoulder of the road and safely out of the traffic flow.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Once stopped, what should you do besides applying the parking brake and shifting to neutral or park?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely
choice_b: Cancel your turn signal and activate your four-way emergency flashers
choice_c: Exit the vehicle immediately
choice_d: Sound the horn three times
explanation: The manual states that once stopped, you should cancel your turn signal and activate your four-way emergency flashers, in addition to applying the parking brake and shifting to neutral/park.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: What should you do with your feet once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver?
choice_a: Keep steady pressure on the brake pedal at all times
choice_b: Remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals
choice_c: Keep the clutch pedal fully depressed
choice_d: Rest one foot on the accelerator
explanation: The manual instructs you to remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals once stopped.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, which turn signal should you activate?
choice_a: The four-way flashers only, with no turn signal
choice_b: The left turn signal
choice_c: The right turn signal
choice_d: No signal is needed since you are pulling back onto the road
explanation: The manual states that when instructed to resume, you should turn off your four-way flashers and activate the left turn signal.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Should you turn the steering wheel before your vehicle starts moving when resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver?
choice_a: No, do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves
choice_b: Yes, turn the wheel fully before releasing the parking brake
choice_c: It does not matter as long as you check your mirrors
choice_d: Yes, but only halfway
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs: do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Before entering a curve, what should you do to your speed?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop before entering
choice_b: Maintain exactly the posted expressway speed
choice_c: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_d: Increase speed slightly to maintain momentum through the curve
explanation: The manual instructs that before entering the curve, you should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: What should you do as you approach a curve, before reducing speed?
choice_a: Shift into the highest available gear
choice_b: Move to the innermost lane of the curve
choice_c: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_d: Activate your hazard lights
explanation: The manual states that when approaching a curve, you should check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: Where should you keep the vehicle while going through a curve?
choice_a: Straddling both lanes to maintain visibility
choice_b: On the shoulder for a wider turning radius
choice_c: As close to the centerline as possible for the shortest path
choice_d: In the lane, while continuing to check traffic in all directions
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep the vehicle in the lane and continue checking traffic in all directions while in a curve.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: Before reaching a railroad crossing, what should all commercial drivers do?
choice_a: Decelerate, brake smoothly, shift gears as necessary, and look and listen for the presence of trains
choice_b: Sound the horn continuously until past the crossing
choice_c: Accelerate to clear the crossing more quickly
choice_d: Change into neutral and coast across
explanation: The manual states that before reaching the crossing, all commercial drivers should decelerate, brake smoothly, and shift gears as necessary, and look and listen for the presence of trains.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What is prohibited while any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_a: You must not exceed 5 mph
choice_b: You must not use your turn signals
choice_c: You must not use your mirrors
choice_d: You must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
explanation: The manual states you should not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: Will every on-road test route necessarily include a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Yes, and if none exists the test is automatically failed
choice_b: No, and railroad crossing knowledge is never tested
choice_c: No, not all driving road test routes will have a railroad crossing; you may instead be asked to explain and demonstrate procedures at a simulated location
choice_d: Yes, every route is guaranteed to include one
explanation: The manual states that not all driving road test routes will have a railroad crossing, and you may be asked to explain and demonstrate the proper procedures at a simulated location.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: Which drivers must observe special railroad crossing procedures at every crossing (unless the crossing is exempt)?
choice_a: Only drivers of empty tank trucks
choice_b: Drivers of a bus, a school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards
choice_c: Only drivers exceeding 26,001 pounds GVWR
choice_d: All drivers equally, with no distinction by vehicle type
explanation: The manual states that if you are driving a bus, a school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, you should be prepared to observe special procedures at every railroad crossing (unless the crossing is exempt).
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: As a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, what should be activated?
choice_a: The reverse warning alarm
choice_b: The high beam headlights
choice_c: The four-way flashers
choice_d: The interior cabin lights
explanation: The manual states that as the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, you should activate the four-way flashers.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: Within what distance range from the nearest rail must a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_b: Exactly 20 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Within 100 feet but not less than 25 feet
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states you should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: If operating a bus at a railroad crossing, what additional action may you be required to take before crossing the tracks?
choice_a: Deploy the wheelchair lift
choice_b: Radio dispatch for clearance
choice_c: Open the window and door
choice_d: Turn off the headlights
explanation: The manual states that if operating a bus, you may also be required to open the window and door prior to crossing tracks.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What should you keep your hands on as the vehicle crosses the tracks?
choice_a: The steering wheel
choice_b: The window crank
choice_c: The gear shift lever
choice_d: The parking brake handle
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep hands on the steering wheel as the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: When should the four-way flashers be deactivated after a railroad crossing?
choice_a: After the vehicle crosses the tracks
choice_b: Before reaching the tracks
choice_c: While still stopped at the tracks
choice_d: They should remain on for the rest of the route
explanation: The manual states the four-way flashers should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass, what might the examiner ask you?
choice_a: What the posted weight limit was
choice_b: What the speed limit on the overpass was
choice_c: What the posted clearance or height was
choice_d: How many lanes the overpass had
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After going over a bridge, what might the examiner ask you?
choice_a: What color the bridge was painted
choice_b: What the posted clearance was
choice_c: What the posted weight limit was
choice_d: How long the bridge was
explanation: The manual states that after going over a bridge, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: If your test route does not have a bridge or overpass, what might you be asked about instead?
choice_a: The examiner's personal driving history
choice_b: Nothing; this portion of the test is simply skipped
choice_c: The vehicle's registration information
choice_d: Another traffic sign that may appear on the route, which you should be prepared to identify and explain
explanation: The manual states that if your route does not have a bridge or overpass, you may be asked about another traffic sign, and should be prepared to identify and explain it.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: Who is required to demonstrate a student discharge during the on-road test?
choice_a: All CDL applicants regardless of endorsement
choice_b: Only applicants renewing an existing CDL
choice_c: Applicants applying for a School Bus endorsement
choice_d: Only applicants under the age of 21
explanation: The manual states that if you are applying for a School Bus endorsement, you will be required to demonstrate a student discharge.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As you approach the student pick-up point, what lights and signals should you activate?
choice_a: High beam headlights only
choice_b: Red warning lights and left turn signals
choice_c: Amber warning lights and right turn signals
choice_d: Four-way flashers only
explanation: The manual states that as you approach the student pick up, you must activate amber warning lights and right turn signals.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: How far from the students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop for a student discharge?
choice_a: At least 50 feet away from students at the stop
choice_b: At least 10 feet away from students at the stop
choice_c: At least 5 feet away from students at the stop
choice_d: At least 25 feet away from students at the stop
explanation: The manual states you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10' away from students at the stop.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: What must be activated once you have stopped for student discharge?
choice_a: The four-way flashers only
choice_b: The high beam headlights
choice_c: The amber warning lights only
choice_d: The stop arm and red warning lights
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for the student discharge, you must activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: What gear and brake actions must you take as you stop for a student discharge?
choice_a: Place the transmission in neutral/park and set the parking brake
choice_b: Leave the transmission in drive with your foot on the brake
choice_c: Turn off the engine entirely
choice_d: Shift into reverse to signal a stop
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for the student discharge, you must place the transmission in neutral/park and set the parking brake.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When actually discharging students, what four actions are required?
choice_a: Turn off the engine, exit the bus, and personally escort each student
choice_b: Radio the school office, log the time, open the door, and check mirrors only
choice_c: Communicate to students, check traffic, open the student door, and check for students
choice_d: Sound the horn, flash headlights, open all doors, and wave students forward
explanation: The manual states that when discharging students, you must communicate to students, check traffic, open the student door, and check for students.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When students are crossing the road during a student discharge, what must you do?
choice_a: Turn off the stop arm and red lights immediately
choice_b: Check traffic, communicate to students, and check for students
choice_c: Close the student door as soon as the first student exits
choice_d: Begin slowly moving the bus forward to save time
explanation: The manual states that when students are crossing, you must check traffic, communicate to students, and check for students.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: What must you do when resuming from a student discharge stop?
choice_a: Sound the horn once and proceed without further checks
choice_b: Check all mirrors, turn off warning lights and stop arm, close the door, check traffic, and accelerate away from the stop area
choice_c: Immediately accelerate to the posted speed limit
choice_d: Leave the stop arm extended until the next intersection
explanation: The manual states that when resuming from the student discharge, you must check all mirrors, turn off warning lights and stop arm, close the door, check traffic, and accelerate away from the stop area.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: For a manual transmission vehicle, what should you always use to shift gears?
choice_a: The clutch
choice_b: Only the accelerator, without the clutch
choice_c: The parking brake
choice_d: Engine braking exclusively
explanation: The manual states you should always use the clutch to shift on a manual transmission.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: If your vehicle is equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, what technique must you use when shifting?
choice_a: You must shift without using the clutch at all
choice_b: You must coast between every gear change
choice_c: You must single-clutch and shift quickly
choice_d: You must double-clutch when shifting
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which of the following clutch habits should you avoid?
choice_a: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
choice_b: Using the clutch to start the engine
choice_c: Fully depressing the clutch only when shifting gears
choice_d: Releasing the clutch smoothly after each shift
explanation: The manual states you should not ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which gear-related behavior should be avoided while shifting a manual transmission?
choice_a: Downshifting before a stop
choice_b: Selecting the gear that matches engine RPM
choice_c: Using the clutch during a shift
choice_d: Grinding or clashing gears
explanation: The manual instructs you to not grind or clash gears.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What kind of gear should you select while driving?
choice_a: The lowest gear available at all times
choice_b: Whichever gear was last used, regardless of engine sound
choice_c: A gear that does not rev or lug the engine
choice_d: The highest gear available at all times
explanation: The manual instructs you to select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Where should you avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: While merging onto an expressway
choice_b: While stopped at a red light
choice_c: On straight sections of expressway
choice_d: In turns and intersections
explanation: The manual instructs you to not shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which brake habit should you avoid?
choice_a: Braking before entering a curve
choice_b: Applying steady, smooth pressure to the brake
choice_c: Riding or pumping the brake
choice_d: Releasing the brake gradually when stopping
explanation: The manual instructs you to not ride or pump the brake.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: How should you brake according to the general driving behavior guidance?
choice_a: In short, rapid pulses regardless of speed
choice_b: Smoothly, using steady pressure, without braking harshly
choice_c: Only with the parking brake, not the service brake
choice_d: As hard as possible every time to ensure a full stop
explanation: The manual states you should not brake harshly, and should brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: Which of the following must you avoid driving the vehicle over?
choice_a: Curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings
choice_b: Manhole covers only
choice_c: Painted crosswalks only
choice_d: Speed bumps only
explanation: The manual instructs you to not put the vehicle over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: On a multiple lane road, in which lane should you finish a left turn?
choice_a: The lane farthest from the center line
choice_b: The center turn lane
choice_c: The lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_d: Any lane, as long as it is not the right-most lane
explanation: The manual states you should complete a turn in the proper lane on a multiple lane road, with the vehicle finishing a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: In which lane should you finish a right turn?
choice_a: The left-most lane
choice_b: The center lane
choice_c: The right-most (curb) lane
choice_d: Any available lane
explanation: The manual states you should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Which lane should you move to or remain in generally, according to the lane usage guidance?
choice_a: The right-most lane, unless the lane is blocked
choice_b: The center lane on a three-lane road
choice_c: The left-most lane at all times
choice_d: Whichever lane has the least traffic regardless of position
explanation: The manual instructs you to move to or remain in the right-most lane unless the lane is blocked.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Which steering behavior should you avoid?
choice_a: Checking mirrors while driving straight
choice_b: Keeping both hands on the wheel while turning
choice_c: Over-steering or under-steering the vehicle
choice_d: Returning both hands to the wheel after shifting
explanation: The manual instructs you to not over or under steer the vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: When should both hands be on the steering wheel, according to the steering guidance?
choice_a: At all times, unless shifting; hands should return to the wheel once the shift is complete
choice_b: Only when instructed by the examiner
choice_c: Only while making turns
choice_d: Only on the expressway
explanation: The manual states you should keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and once you have completed the shift, return both hands to the steering wheel.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

topic: General Driving Behaviors - Regular Traffic Checks
question: According to the Regular Traffic Checks guidance, when should you check mirrors and traffic in relation to an intersection?
choice_a: Only after leaving the intersection
choice_b: Only before entering the intersection
choice_c: Before, while in, and after an intersection
choice_d: Only if a traffic signal is present
explanation: The manual states you should check mirrors and traffic before, while in, and after an intersection.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

topic: General Driving Behaviors - Regular Traffic Checks
question: In which areas should you scan and check traffic with extra care?
choice_a: Only on the expressway
choice_b: Only during the Basic Control Skills exercises
choice_c: High volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present
choice_d: Only in rural areas with low traffic
explanation: The manual instructs you to scan and check traffic in high volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

topic: General Driving Behaviors - Use of Turn Signals
question: When should turn signals be activated, according to the Use of Turn Signals guidance?
choice_a: Only when requested by the examiner
choice_b: When required and at appropriate times
choice_c: Only on multi-lane roads
choice_d: Only when another vehicle is nearby
explanation: The manual instructs you to activate turn signals when required and at appropriate times.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals

topic: General Driving Behaviors - Use of Turn Signals
question: When should you cancel your turn signal?
choice_a: Only after coming to a complete stop
choice_b: Only when the examiner reminds you
choice_c: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
choice_d: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
explanation: The manual states you should cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals
